name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority
why: Exact match. Full sentence continues '...alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.' The page also points to aistatement.com.

name: Future of Life Institute (FLI)
quote: AI experts rate leading AI companies on key safety and security domains.
why: Exact match. Qualifies as a lab rater.

name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
quote: The default consequence of the creation of artificial superintelligence (ASI) is human extinction.

name: SaferAI
quote: We rate frontier AI companies' risk management practices.
why: Exact match. Ratings sit on the tracker.safer-ai.org subdomain.

name: The Midas Project
quote: The Seoul Tracker evaluates sixteen leading AI companies
why: Exact match (sentence continues '...that promised to implement safety frameworks at the 2024 AI Seoul Summit'). Also says no company earned better than 'B-' and six got 'F'.

name: ControlAI
quote: We seriously risk human extinction by building superintelligence.
why: The draft quote ('extinction of the human race') did not match: the fetch returned 'extinction of the humanity', so the wording is uncertain. Replaced it with an unambiguous sentence. Confirmed: controlai.com returns a 302 redirect to controlai.org.

name: PauseAI (Global)
why: The draft quote on /xrisk was CAIS's wording, cited there, not PauseAI's own voice. Replaced it with the homepage line: 'We are risking human extinction. We need to pause AI development, right now.'

name: PauseAI US
quote: a technology that could cause mass unemployment, catastrophic accidents, and even human extinction
why: The draft quote from /about/ was a line about opinion polls, not an organizational warning. Replaced it with the homepage sentence 'AI companies are racing to build a technology that could cause...'.

name: Redwood Research
quote: a bedrock approach for mitigating catastrophic risk from misaligned AI
why: Exact match ('AI control has been framed as a bedrock approach...'). The homepage also says 'could enable future AIs to take over.' It is written in a research voice rather than as a public campaign.

name: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
doc: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks (co-authored paper)
quote: Further progress in AI development could lead to capabilities that pose extreme risks
why: The quote is verbatim but comes from a paper led by DeepMind (Shevlane et al.) with GovAI co-authors, and its 'extreme risks' examples are cyber and manipulation. The about page ('help decision-makers ... navigate the transition to a world with advanced AI') has no catastrophic or loss-of-control warning. Its research list covers catastrophic misuse (power grid, bioterrorism) but nothing on extinction or loss of control. Legal entity: US 501(c)(3) with UK subsidiary; offices in London and DC.

name: Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR)
doc: AI loss of control incidents are worsening (29 Aug 2026)
quote: AI loss of control incidents are worsening significantly.
why: Exact match. The report also says 'including ones with catastrophic consequences'. CLTR manages the Loss of Control Observatory.

name: Centre for the Study of Existential Risk (CSER)
quote: could also potentially pose catastrophic risks from accidents (safety) or misuse (security)
why: This AI-specific page replaces the draft's generic mission quote, which was verbatim on /about-us/ but not about AI. The wording is hedged. The page belongs to a University of Cambridge centre.

name: AI Futures Project
why: Verbatim, and the page credits the AI Futures Project, so it is the org's own named publication. Caveat: the quote is scenario narrative, not a direct statement. aifutures.org itself has no warning language. The ai-futures.org redirect was not checked.

name: Encode
quote: We believe AI could cause catastrophic risks
why: The draft dropped 'We believe'. The full sentence adds 'whether through deliberate misuse or the loss of human control', 16 words total, so it was trimmed.

name: CeSIA (Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA)
doc: Global Call for AI Red Lines (co-organizer)
quote: increasingly difficult to exert meaningful human control in the coming years
why: Exact match. red-lines.ai names CeSIA as one of three launch organizers, with The Future Society and CHAI, so this is a joint campaign. CeSIA's own site (cesia.org/en/, Paris, no redirect seen) says only 'dedicated to preventing major risks associated with AI'. The securite-ia.fr redirect was not checked.

name: Palisade Research
quote: avoid permanent disempowerment by strategic AI agents
why: Exact match. The page also says 'nobody has a credible plan to prevent humans from losing control of superintelligence'. It confirms a Berkeley, CA location.

name: Existential Risk Observatory
quote: Future artificial intelligence (AI) with goals that may be different from ours
why: Verbatim item in a list introduced by 'The most important existential risks as recent research identifies them are:'. The draft's blog post ('Yes RAND, AI Could Really Cause Human Extinction') could not be fetched because of a robots.txt error, so its title is unverified; a manual browser check would give a stronger quote. HQ NL (Amsterdam per draft; not confirmed on the page).

name: AISafety.info (Stampy)
doc: 6: AI's goals may not match ours
quote: Create a superintelligent AI with the wrong goals? Your species goes extinct.
why: Exact match. The page also says 'the default outcome is a catastrophe.' Fiscally sponsored by Ashgro (US).
